Control section for particle-size classes and their substitutes (USDA)

Source: R/familia-usda-particle-size.R
family_control_section_usda.Rd

The key to the control section for particle-size classes and their substitutes in mineral soils of the Keys to Soil Taxonomy (13th ed., 2022, ch. 17, pp. 357-358), cases A to G: a root-limiting layer within 36 cm (A); Andisols (B); Alfisols, Ultisols and the Aridisols and Mollisols with an argillic, kandic or natric horizon starting within 100 cm and ending at 25 cm or deeper, or in Arenic or Grossarenic subgroups (C, items 1 to 4); the same orders with that horizon at 100 cm or deeper or in Lamellic subgroups (D); an argillic or natric horizon ending above 25 cm (E); Wassents (F); and all other mineral soils, from the Ap horizon or 25 cm to 100 cm or a root-limiting layer (G). Depths are from the mineral soil surface (or the top of organic material with andic soil properties, when shallower).

Usage

family_control_section_usda(
  pedon,
  order_code = NULL,
  great_group = NULL,
  subgroup = NULL
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

order_code

USDA order code (e.g. "AF"), or NULL.

great_group

Great group name (e.g. "Hapludalfs"), or NULL.

subgroup

Subgroup name (e.g. "Arenic Hapludalfs"), or NULL.

Value

A list: top, bottom (cm), case (A to G, with the item of case C, e.g. "C4"), evidence and missing.

Details

Root-limiting layers (p. 357) are field observations: one not recorded is absent. When a test that decides the case is undecided, the bounds are NA and the missing columns are listed.

References

Soil Survey Staff (2022). Keys to Soil Taxonomy, 13th ed. USDA-NRCS. Chapter 17, pp. 357-358.

Examples

p <- make_luvisol_canonical()
family_control_section_usda(p, order_code = "AF",
                            great_group = "Hapludalfs",
                            subgroup = "Typic Hapludalfs")[c("top", "bottom", "case")]
#> $top
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> $bottom
#> [1] 75
#> 
#> $case
#> [1] "C4"
#>
